extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and members of the mathematical community (researchers, graduate students, evaluators) interested in how to judge mathematical work
extracted.subtask_description: A framework for judging mathematical research by distinguishing the values of two coexisting cultures (theory-builders vs problem-solvers) and applying the culture-internal criteria appropriate to the work being evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long programs that organize and unify
rubrics_metrics.description: Long programs that organize and unify (Grothendieck, Langlands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued by theory-builders: look for sustained efforts that create an organizing framework across areas. Such programs are judged by how well they systematize and connect disparate results into a coherent whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual abstractions that subsume many phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Conceptual abstractions that subsume many phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory-builders prize definitions and concepts that capture a wide range of examples; evaluate whether the abstraction reveals deeper structure and explains multiple previously separate facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Right" definitions; the right framework is half the work
rubrics_metrics.description: "Right" definitions; the right framework is half the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the choice of definitions and framework simplifies problems, clarifies relationships, and makes subsequent progress natural rather than ad hoc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality: results that apply across categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Generality; results that apply across categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge theorems by their scope and applicability across contexts (functoriality, category-spanning statements). General statements that capture many cases are prized by theory-builders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness: full structural theorems
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the work attains a comprehensive structural description or classification rather than isolated partial results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty as harmony and inevitability of the framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty in the sense of harmony and inevitability of the framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For theory-oriented work, aesthetic value lies in how naturally the results and definitions fit together and how ‘‘inevitable’’ the development seems in hindsight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single hard concrete problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Single hard concrete problems (Riemann hypothesis, Erdős-style combinatorics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem-solvers value the resolution of specific, well-known, difficult problems; assess importance by the difficulty and prominence of the problem solved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bare-hands ingenuity; new tricks not yet absorbed into a theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Bare-hands ingenuity; new tricks that are not yet absorbed into a theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for clever ad hoc methods or ingenious ideas that produce results even if they don't yet fit into a grander conceptual framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharp constants and best-possible bounds
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether results obtain quantitatively optimal bounds, precise thresholds, or best-possible estimates — a primary virtue for problem-focused work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise; counter-intuitive results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem-solvers prize unexpected outcomes or constructions that overturn intuition; such results are valued for revealing hidden structure or limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty as clever technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty in the sense of clever technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aesthetic merit for problem-solving work is often the elegance or novelty of the technique used to obtain the result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated power of a method by what it solves, not by what it organizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated power of a method by what it solves, not by what it organizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess methods by the concrete problems they can handle; success is measured in solved problems and effective tricks rather than in unifying principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (theory-builder version)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using the theory-builder lens, judge depth by the ability of work to exhibit deep connections and structural insights across different areas of mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth (problem-solver version)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth (problem-solver version): Reveals new combinatorial structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the problem-solver perspective, depth is shown by uncovering new fine-grained structure in concrete objects or problems; look for novel combinatorial or arithmetic phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance (theory-builder vs problem-solver)
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance: theory-builder — subsumes many subfields; problem-solver — settles a long-open conjecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine importance relative to the culture: theoretical importance is judged by unifying power, while problem-oriented importance is judged by resolution of longstanding, high-profile problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality (table contrast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Generality: theory-builder — functorial, abstract; problem-solver — sharp, explicit constants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the contribution's primary virtue is abstract generality across contexts or precise, concrete quantitative strength in specific settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress (theory-builder vs problem-solver)
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress: theory-builder — new theory absorbs old work; problem-solver — new trick solves old problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether progress is conceptual (creates frameworks that explain prior results) or instrumental (provides new techniques that directly resolve problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test of value (table contrast)
rubrics_metrics.description: Test of value: theory-builder — tools become universal; problem-solver — bound is tight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use culture-appropriate tests: for theory, value is shown if the ideas become widely used; for problem-solving, value is shown by optimal/definitive results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use culture-internal criteria when evaluating
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating a piece of mathematics, ask which culture it belongs to and apply that culture's criteria rather than imposing the other culture's standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cross-cultural snobbery: do not dismiss combinatorial/ problem-solving work for lacking grand abstraction, nor dismiss theory work for being non-technical. Both cultures are legitimate and necessary.
